objectives: Describe the UN and its main organs
Describe the OAU and the African Union
Describe the Commonwealth and La Francophonie
Explain Cameroon's membership and regional groupings
reviewNotes: Teacher to verify: UN founding (1945) and Cameroon's UN admission (1960), the OAU date (May 1963, Addis Ababa), the AU's replacement of the OAU (2002), Cameroon's Commonwealth membership (1990s) and the CEMAC membership list.

Draft for teacher review: only well-established facts are used and the tone is neutral; every date and name must be verified against the official History syllabus and standard references before release.

blocks.md: Countries cooperate through **international organisations**. The **United Nations (UN)**, founded in **1945**, aims to keep peace, protect human rights and promote development. Its main organs include the **General Assembly** (all members), the **Security Council** (responsible for peace and security), the **International Court of Justice**, the **Secretariat** and agencies such as **UNESCO**, **WHO** and **UNICEF**. Cameroon joined the UN in 1960.

blocks.caption: International organisations
blocks.alt: A timeline from 1944 to 2004 with the UN in 1945, the OAU in 1963 and the AU in 2002.

blocks.title: OAU and AU
blocks.md: The **Organisation of African Unity (OAU)** was founded in **May 1963** at **Addis Ababa**. Its aims were African unity, defence of independence, end of colonialism and apartheid, and cooperation. The **African Union (AU)** replaced it in **2002**, with broader aims, such as peace, democracy, economic integration and human rights, and a Peace and Security Council.

blocks.title: Commonwealth and Francophonie
blocks.md: The **Commonwealth** is an association of countries, most of them former British colonies, which cooperate in education, trade and democracy. The **Francophonie** is a similar association of countries that share the French language and cultural ties. **Cameroon** is a member of both, which reflects its two colonial histories (it joined the Commonwealth in the 1990s).

**Regional groupings** in Africa aim to promote trade and cooperation: **CEMAC** in Central Africa (Cameroon, Chad, the Central African Republic, Congo, Equatorial Guinea and Gabon) and **ECOWAS** in West Africa. Benefits include larger markets, free movement of goods and shared projects such as roads. Difficulties include weak infrastructure, similar economies, political disputes and shortages of money.

blocks.title: Be careful
blocks.md:
- The AU replaced the OAU in 2002; they are not the same organisation, but the AU grew out of the OAU.
- Membership of the Commonwealth does not mean being ruled by Britain; members are independent states.
- Regional groupings are not the same as the UN: they cover a smaller area with specific aims.

blocks.title: Example 1: organs of the UN
blocks.statement: Which UN organ includes all members and which is responsible for peace and security?
steps: The General Assembly includes all members.
The Security Council deals with peace and security.

blocks.title: Example 2: OAU to AU
blocks.statement: Name the city where the OAU was founded and the year the AU replaced it.
steps: The OAU was founded in Addis Ababa in 1963.

lessons.title: The Cold War in outline and its effect on Africa

objectives: Define the Cold War and name the two blocs
Explain how the Cold War affected Africa
Describe the end of the Cold War
reviewNotes: Teacher to verify: dates (NATO 1949, Warsaw Pact 1955, Berlin Wall 1961 and 1989, Cuban crisis 1962, USSR dissolved in December 1991) and the examples of African conflicts; the lesson uses neutral wording about both blocs.

Draft for teacher review: only well-established facts are used and the tone is neutral; every date and name must be verified against the official History syllabus and standard references before release.

blocks.md: The **Cold War** was a long rivalry after the Second World War between two superpowers, the **United States** and the **Soviet Union (USSR)**, and their allies. It was called 'cold' because the two sides never fought each other directly in a full war, but competed through **arms races**, propaganda, spying, economic aid and **proxy wars** in other countries. It lasted from about **1945 to 1991**.

blocks.caption: Cold War blocs
blocks.alt: Two columns summarising the Western and Eastern blocs.

blocks.title: Two blocs
blocks.md: The **Western bloc** led by the USA was **capitalist and democratic** and formed **NATO** in 1949. The **Eastern bloc** led by the USSR was **communist** and formed the **Warsaw Pact** in 1955. Germany was divided, and Berlin too; the **Berlin Wall** was built in 1961 and fell in **1989**. The **Cuban Missile Crisis** of 1962 brought the world close to nuclear war.

**Effects on Africa.** Both blocs tried to win friends among the new African states. They gave **aid, weapons and advisers**, and some wars in Africa (such as in Angola) became linked to the rivalry. Some African states chose one side, others followed **non-alignment**, refusing to join either bloc. African leaders also used the rivalry to get aid. The UN and the OAU worked for peace and decolonisation.

blocks.title: The end
blocks.md: In **1989–1991** communist governments in eastern Europe collapsed, the Berlin Wall fell and in **December 1991** the **Soviet Union** broke up. The Cold War ended. In Africa the end brought new demands for **multiparty democracy** and changes in aid, although also new conflicts and economic challenges.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- 'Cold' does not mean a climate: it means no direct large-scale war between the superpowers.
- Non-alignment is not neutrality in all matters; it means not joining a military bloc.
- Keep to the dates: NATO 1949, Berlin Wall 1961, Cuban crisis 1962, USSR ends 1991.

blocks.title: Example 1: blocs
blocks.statement: Name the leaders of the two blocs and an organisation for each.
steps: The USA led the Western bloc, which formed NATO.
The USSR led the Eastern bloc, which formed the Warsaw Pact.
blocks.answer: USA with NATO; USSR with the Warsaw Pact.

blocks.title: Example 2: effect on Africa
blocks.statement: Give one way in which the Cold War affected an African state.
steps: Both blocs offered aid and weapons.
Some conflicts became linked to the rivalry.
So an African state might receive aid or be drawn into a proxy war.
blocks.answer: Aid and weapons; involvement in proxy wars.
